# SPE Round 01 Plan: triage agent

The spec for this round is your prompt: "triage tickets correctly and cheaply." This plan is the round 01 prediction. After you approve it, I will save the prediction, build the harness, and run one Workflow as the eval. I will commit locally after each step. I will not push.

Some details were missing, so I chose these defaults:
- The 40 tickets and reference labels live in `data/tickets.jsonl`. I will copy them into `spe/evals/` and split the text from the labels.
- "Cheaply" means a mean cost under $0.010 per ticket. This is logged as decision D1 for you to confirm.
- The agent under test uses the current Sonnet and Haiku model IDs. I will check the IDs against the Claude API docs before the harness commit.

## 0. Setup (before Specify)

1. Create `spe/` with the folders listed in the SPE way.
2. Save your prompt and planning answers verbatim to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md`.
3. Build the first version of the agent in `triage/`:
   - `triage/prompt.md` holds the system prompt with definitions for the 5 categories and the 4 priorities.
   - `triage/schema.json` holds the output schema: `category`, `priority`, `reply_draft`, `needs_human` (boolean).
   - `triage/run.js` makes one API call per ticket with structured output and no tools.

## 1. Specify

### Requirement table (round 01)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R01 | Assign one category from billing, bug, how-to, account, outage | User: "triage tickets correctly" | Code: exact match to the reference category |
| R02 | Assign one priority from P1 to P4 | User: "triage tickets correctly" | Code: exact match to the reference priority |
| R03 | Never rate a reference P1 ticket lower than P2 | Decision D2 | Code: P1 recall at P1 or P2 |
| R04 | Output is valid JSON that matches `triage/schema.json` | Decision D3 | Code: schema validation |
| R05 | Draft a first reply that answers the ticket and invents no refunds, credits, dates, or policy | User: "drafts a first reply" in the project brief | Judge with a 4-item rubric, blind to config |
| R06 | Mean cost per ticket is under $0.010 | User: "cheaply", Decision D1 | Code: summed token usage times list price |
| R07 | The agent never sees reference labels | SPE way | Code: transcript scan for label file paths or label strings |

### Disagreements and defaults (`spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Decision | Default I will use | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | What "cheaply" means | Under $0.010 per ticket on average | You |
| D2 | How much a missed outage costs | A P1 rated P3 or P4 counts as a severe failure | You |
| D3 | Output format | JSON that matches a fixed schema | Claude (logged default) |
| D4 | Whether the reference labels are always right | Labels are truth for this round. Tickets where all 3 configs agree against the label go on a list for the support lead | You and the support lead |
| D5 | Where ticket text may go | Tickets stay local and go only to the Claude API | You |

There are no proposals from a previous round to adopt or reject because this is round 01.

## 2. Predict

### Configurations

Each config changes one thing from C0.

| Config | Model | Prompt | What changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| C0 | Sonnet (current) | Definitions only, zero-shot | Baseline |
| C1 | Sonnet (current) | Definitions plus 10 written examples | Adds few-shot examples. The examples are new text that I write from the definitions. None of them comes from the 40 eval tickets. |
| C2 | Haiku (current) | Definitions only, zero-shot | Swaps in a cheaper model |
| Naive | None | Always predict the most common category and priority in the eval set | Floor for comparison |

### Predictions

A hit means the measured value falls inside the band. With 40 tickets, one ticket moves accuracy by 0.025. Each config runs 3 trials per ticket.

| Metric | C0 | C1 | C2 | Naive | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Schema valid rate | 0.98 ± 0.02 | 0.98 ± 0.02 | 0.95 ± 0.04 | n/a | `check_schema` | Structured output almost always parses. A smaller model drops fields slightly more often. |
| Category accuracy | 0.85 ± 0.06 | 0.88 ± 0.06 | 0.78 ± 0.08 | 0.30 ± 0.10 | `check_category_exact` | Most tickets name their topic. Errors will come from bug versus outage and account versus billing. |
| Priority exact accuracy | 0.60 ± 0.10 | 0.68 ± 0.10 | 0.52 ± 0.10 | 0.35 ± 0.10 | `check_priority_exact` | The support lead uses unwritten rules for priority. Examples teach some of them. |
| Priority within one level | 0.92 ± 0.05 | 0.94 ± 0.05 | 0.88 ± 0.06 | 0.75 ± 0.10 | `check_priority_within_one` | Disagreements on priority are usually one level apart. |
| P1 recall (rated P1 or P2) | 0.85 ± 0.15 | 0.90 ± 0.15 | 0.75 ± 0.15 | 0.00 ± 0.05 | `check_p1_recall` | Outage words are strong signals. The band is wide because the set likely holds only about 4 P1 tickets. |
| Reply draft pass rate | 0.80 ± 0.10 | 0.82 ± 0.10 | 0.70 ± 0.10 | n/a | `judge_reply` (4-item rubric) | Drafts will read well. The most common failure will be a promised fix date or credit. |
| Mean cost per ticket (USD, estimate) | 0.010 ± 0.004 | 0.014 ± 0.005 | 0.003 ± 0.0015 | 0.000 | `check_cost` | The examples add about 1,500 input tokens. Haiku costs a fraction of Sonnet per token. |

These numbers are estimates made before any measurement. The naive accuracy numbers depend on the label mix. If the mix differs a lot from my guess, I will note that in the log. I will not edit the prediction.

### Prediction file

`spe/predictions/r01.yaml` will hold these numbers, the bands, each Why, and `same_as_last_round: null` because this is round 01.

## 3. Evaluate

### Files

- `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl` holds ticket text only.
- `spe/evals/answers/labels.jsonl` holds the reference labels. Only graders read it.
- `spe/evals/graders/` holds the code checks and the judge rubric.
- `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js` is the Workflow script. It holds `const ROUND = 1` and builds every round label from that constant.

### Harness steps and gates

| Step | What it does | Gate to pass before the next step |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Grader selftest | The oracle file (the labels themselves) scores 1.0. An empty output file fails every check. A wrong file with shifted labels scores below 0.30. |
| 2 | Control regrade | Round 01 has no last round. I will regrade the oracle file and one fixed hand-written answer file twice, and both runs must give identical scores. |
| 3 | Dry run | 1 ticket times 3 configs gives 3 cells. Each output must pass the schema, get graded, and log cost. |
| 4 | Full run | 40 tickets times 3 configs times 3 trials gives 360 trials. Code checks run first. |
| 5 | Split cells | When the 3 trials of a cell disagree on category or priority, the cell gets up to 2 extra trials. Extra trials stop at 60 in total. |
| 6 | Judge pass | One Opus judge grades reply drafts only. It sees the ticket and the draft but not the config name. |
| 7 | Leak scan | Scan every transcript for the labels path or label strings. Void any trial that matches and log it. |
| 8 | Failure analysis | Group every miss into F-numbered failure types with examples. |
| 9 | Completeness critic | A separate agent checks that every requirement row has a measured number and that every voided or skipped trial is logged. |

### Workflow arguments

```
ROUND: 1
configs: [C0, C1, C2]
tickets: spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl
trials_per_cell: 3
extra_trials_per_split_cell: 2
extra_trials_cap: 60
spend_cap_usd: 20
judge_model: Opus (current)
```

The Workflow skips any trial that would push spend past the $20 cap and logs each skip.

### Cost estimate (not measured)

| Item | Estimate |
|---|---|
| C0, 120 trials | $1.20 |
| C1, 120 trials | $1.70 |
| C2, 120 trials | $0.40 |
| Extra trials, up to 60 | $0.60 |
| Judge, about 420 drafts | $8.00 |
| Total | about $12, capped at $20 |

## 4. Steps after approval

1. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`.
2. Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`. The first line is `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` The author is "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode".
3. Commit `SPE r01 specify` with the transcript, `spec.md`, and `disagreements.md`.
4. Commit `SPE r01 predict: baseline, few-shot, and Haiku configs` with the plan copy and the prediction file. This commit lands before any harness work.
5. Build the agent, the graders, and the Workflow script. Commit `SPE r01 evaluate (harness)`.
6. Launch the Workflow. It returns at launch, and I close out when its completion notice arrives.
7. Commit `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <headline>` with the measured numbers.
8. Write `spe/prediction-log.md`, `spe/failures.md`, the "Proposed for round 02" table, `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`, and `spe/README.md`. Commit `SPE r01 learn: <headline>` and tag `spe-r01` locally.

Commit messages will carry no Claude attribution. Nothing gets pushed.

## 5. Halt conditions

I will stop and report to you if any of these happens:
- Spend reaches the $20 cap.
- A trial reads the labels or the prediction file.
- The grader selftest fails.
- A decision only you can make blocks the run, such as D1 or D4.

If every config passes every check, round 02 will need harder tickets or stricter graders.
critiques: The plan quotes the prompt as the spec. It turns the prompt into requirements R01 to R07, and each row has a Test column, for example 'Code: exact match to the reference category' and 'Code: summed token usage times list price'.

The Predictions table gives a number and a band for each config on each metric, for example category accuracy 'C0 0.85 ± 0.06, C1 0.88 ± 0.06, C2 0.78 ± 0.08'. It uses no adjectives in place of numbers.

Every metric row has a Why column that explains the numbers across configs, for example 'The examples add about 1,500 input tokens. Haiku costs a fraction of Sonnet per token.' The reasons are given per row, not per cell, but they cover the differences between configs.

Steps 1, 2, and 4 copy the plan to spe/plans/r01.md and write spe/predictions/r01.yaml. They commit both in 'SPE r01 predict', which 'lands before any harness work', and the Workflow launches later in step 6.

The eval is one Workflow (r01-workflow.js). Its gated steps include step 1 'Grader selftest', with oracle, empty, and shifted-label files, and step 3 'Dry run' with 1 ticket times 3 configs. Both run before the step 4 full run.
The Predictions table has a 'Grader check' column. It ties each metric to a named check such as check_schema, check_p1_recall, judge_reply, or check_cost.

Step 8 writes spe/prediction-log.md and spe/failures.md, a 'Proposed for round 02' table, and spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml, then commits the learn step. The plan never says in so many words that the log compares predicted bands with measured values. The earlier hit definition and the log note imply it, so the step counts as a comparison plus a seed for round 02.
